title: Agents may extend inherited Sky Core logic but not modify it, and Grove has so far declared no customizations
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.5.1.2.1.2.1.1 defines the escape valve for inherited logic: "The Prime Agent may define instance-specific customization of the routine protocol to **extend** the baseline functionality defined in the Sky Core Atlas. This can include custom routines or processes **layered on top of** the inherited Sky Core logic. Any extensions must remain fully aligned with the requirements specified in the Sky Core Atlas." The document then records: "[No customization presently.]"

The verbs carry the constraint. "Extend" and "layered on top of" permit addition; nothing permits replacement or subtraction. An Agent can add a step, a check or a report, but cannot remove or weaken an inherited one — which is what makes automatic propagation safe. If Agents could override the base class, a Sky Core fix could be locally nullified and the inheritance guarantee would be worthless.

The alignment clause adds a substantive ceiling on top of the structural one, mirroring A.6.1.1.2.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.6: even a purely additive extension is invalid if it is misaligned with the Core Atlas. An Agent cannot achieve a prohibited outcome by bolting on a new routine that frustrates the inherited one.

The recorded absence of customization is itself informative. The extension point exists, is documented, and is deliberately empty — so the Artifact distinguishes "no customization exists" from "customization was never considered," which matters for anyone auditing whether Grove's behaviour is fully described by Sky Core defaults.
description: Customization is confined to routines layered on top of the baseline and must remain fully aligned with the Core Atlas, making the extension point additive rather than an override.
